title: Microsoft 365 Copilot in Word for Mac: easier access to the Researcher agent from the document
summary: Pass: the roadmap facts, licensing and admin controls are supported. The web search path is documented across two cited pages, and the preview Graph automation found does not support this row's group-level scope. Add the companion roadmap citation and acknowledge the differing Microsoft statements about compliance access.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance controls table; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The tenant block is at Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > All agents > agent > Block.
claims.quote: Select Agents > All agents. In the All agents page, select an agent from the list of agents. In the agent details pane that opens, immediately under the agent's name, select Block or Unblock.

claims.claim: POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}/block blocks a Copilot package to prevent its usage.
claims.quote: Block a Copilot package to prevent its usage. POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}/block

claims.where: controls[0].note; Risk assessment; Governance controls; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Researcher availability is managed by blocking the agent for the entire tenant.
claims.quote: For the Researcher and Analyst agents, the Edit users panel is disabled. To manage their availability, block the agent for the entire tenant by using the Block action in the Microsoft 365 admin center.

claims.claim: The Edit users panel is disabled for Researcher and Analyst.
claims.quote: For the Researcher and Analyst agents, the Edit users panel is disabled.

claims.claim: The Graph package block call is a beta API.
claims.quote: APIs under the /beta version are subject to change. Use of these APIs in production applications is not supported.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Cost and licensing; Governance controls
claims.claim: Access to the Graph Package Management API requires a Microsoft Agent 365 licence.
claims.quote: Access to the Package Management API requires a Microsoft Agent 365 license.

claims.claim: The block call requires the delegated permission CopilotPackages.ReadWrite.All.
claims.quote: Delegated (work or school account) | CopilotPackages.ReadWrite.All | Not available.

claims.claim: Licence assignment is at Microsoft 365 admin center > Users > Active users > user > Licenses and Apps > Licenses.
claims.quote: Go to the Users > Active users page. Select the row of the user that you want to assign a license to. In the right pane, select Licenses and Apps. Expand the Licenses section, select the boxes for the licenses that you want to assign

claims.claim: Set-MgUserLicense -UserId $userUPN -AddLicenses @{SkuId = "<SkuId>"} -RemoveLicenses @() assigns the chosen licence to the user.
claims.quote: To assign a license to a user, use the following command in PowerShell. Set-MgUserLicense -UserId $userUPN -AddLicenses @{SkuId = "<SkuId>"} -RemoveLicenses @()

claims.claim: Assigning licences requires at least a License or User Administrator.
claims.quote: You must be at least a License or User Administrator to assign licenses.

claims.claim: The web search policy is at Microsoft 365 Apps admin center > Customization > Policy Management > Policy configurations > policy configuration > Choose the scope > Configure Settings > Allow web search in Copilot.
claims.quote: Cloud Policy overview: Under Customization, select Policy Management. On the Policy configurations page, select Create. On the Choose the scope page ... On the Configure Settings page, select the policies. Web search page: Allow web search in Copilot policy.

claims.claim: The web search policy turns web search on or off for users or user groups across the tenant.
claims.quote: This policy allows IT admins to either turn on or turn off web search for users or user groups across the tenant they manage

claims.claim: The Allow web search in Copilot policy is available only in Cloud Policy service.
claims.quote: Allow web search in Copilot policy, which is available only in Cloud Policy service for Microsoft 365.

claims.claim: Office Apps Administrator is the recommended role for Cloud Policy.
claims.quote: Office Apps Administrator (Recommended) | This role can manage Office apps cloud services, including policy and settings management

claims.claim: No API or automation is documented for this row's group-scoped web search policy.
claims.quote: Searched: Allow web search in Copilot Cloud Policy Microsoft Graph API PowerShell configure. Read web search, Cloud Policy, graph/utcm-copilot-resources and configurationMonitor create pages. TCM supports tenant-level policies only and fails if the setting is in any group-level policy.

claims.claim: No separate Word-specific or per-app switch for Researcher entry points is documented as of November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: Researcher Word per app disable entry points Cloud Policy setting; Researcher Word Mac entry points canvas admin policy default report 497914 497913. Opened Researcher FAQ, agent-actions and Cloud Policy overview; no entry-point-specific UI or API found.

claims.claim: Researcher is included with the Microsoft 365 Copilot licence and available to its licence holders.

claims.quote: Researcher and Analyst are pre-pinned in the app, and any user with a Microsoft 365 Copilot license can run up to 25 combined queries per month.

claims.claim: The Researcher FAQ and June 2025 announcement name no separate meter or charge for Researcher.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance
claims.claim: With web search enabled, Copilot generates search queries and sends them to Bing.
claims.quote: Based on these terms, Copilot generates a search query that it sends to the Bing search service asking for more information.

claims.claim: A generated query may be informed by data in an open document when a user prompts Copilot inside Word.
claims.quote: it may also be informed by data within a Microsoft 365 document ... When a user enters a prompt into Copilot inside a Microsoft 365 application (for example, writing a prompt into Copilot in Microsoft Word while a relevant document is open).

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The Data Protection Addendum does not apply to generated web search queries.
claims.quote: The Microsoft Products and Services Data Protection Addendum (DPA) doesn't apply to the use of generated web search queries in Microsoft Copilot, Microsoft Copilot Chat, or the Bing search service.

claims.claim: The EU Data Boundary does not apply to generated search queries.
claims.quote: Also, HIPAA compliance and the EU Data Boundary don't apply to generated search queries.

claims.quote: The information about web search in this article also applies to Researcher, Analyst, and Cowork in Microsoft Copilot.

claims.claim: Researcher may ask clarifying questions before producing its report.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The FAQ says highly complex Researcher responses take 10 to 45 minutes.
claims.quote: Researcher agent responses typically range from under five minutes for simple queries. Then 10 to 45 minutes for highly complex ones.

claims.claim: Users cannot disable Researcher.
claims.quote: Users can't disable Researcher agent.

claims.claim: Users cannot independently remove Researcher.
claims.quote: Researcher agent is a core part of the Microsoft Copilot experience and users cannot independently remove or unpin it.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The FAQ states that Researcher session content is not directly accessible to admins or compliance tools by default.
claims.quote: By default, no. The content of Researcher sessions isn't directly accessible to admins or compliance tools. Admins can see usage metrics (like how many times it's used) but not the actual conversation content.
claims.fix: After the FAQ statement add: 'The cited web search page also includes Researcher and says admins can search, audit and eDiscover prompts, responses and generated web queries; this differs from the FAQ's statement about session content.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/copilot/plan/manage-public-web-access#web-search-query-logging.

claims.claim: Researcher remains accessible under Tools in Copilot Chat even when Copilot agents are disabled for some or all users.
claims.quote: This tool will remain accessible in Microsoft Copilot Chat under Tools, even when Copilot agents are disabled for some or all users in Microsoft 365 admin center.

claims.claim: In this commercial cloud's case, unconfigured Allow web search in Copilot leaves web search available unless Allow the use of additional optional connected experiences in Office is Disabled.
claims.quote: If the IT admin doesn't configure the Allow web search in Copilot policy, web search will be available to users in both Microsoft Copilot and Microsoft Copilot Chat, unless the IT admin has set the Allow the use of additional optional connected experiences in Office policy to Disabled.

claims.claim: Disabled in Microsoft Copilot Work mode; Enabled in Microsoft Copilot Web mode and Microsoft Copilot Chat disables web search in Researcher.
claims.quote: If the IT admin chooses the Disabled in Microsoft Copilot Work mode; Enabled in Microsoft Copilot Web mode and Microsoft Copilot Chat option, web search in Researcher and Cowork in Microsoft Copilot will be disabled.

claims.claim: Cloud Policy settings take effect when the Office app is restarted.
claims.quote: Policies from Cloud Policy are applied only when the Office app is restarted.

claims.claim: The Researcher FAQ answers sovereign-cloud availability with To be released soon.
claims.quote: Is Researcher agent available in Sovereign Clouds? To be released soon.

claims.claim: The FAQ says there is no existing reporting tool for Copilot agents like Researcher and Analyst.
claims.quote: No. There is no existing reporting tool for Copilot agents like Researcher and Analyst.

claims.claim: The FAQ also says admins can see Researcher usage metrics.
claims.quote: Admins can see usage metrics (like how many times it's used) but not the actual conversation content.
